required_decisions.decision: Option A adds an AuditScope enum with TENANT and PLATFORM, makes AuditLog.tenantId nullable, and retains the existing Tenant relation with cascade semantics only for TENANT rows. The reviewed migration must add a database CHECK enforcing (scope = TENANT AND tenant_id IS NOT NULL) OR (scope = PLATFORM AND tenant_id IS NULL), backfill every existing row to TENANT before making the constraint valid, reject either inconsistent combination below the application layer, add a partial tenant query index on (tenant_id, created_at DESC) WHERE scope = TENANT, and add a partial platform chronology index on (created_at DESC) WHERE scope = PLATFORM. Prisma schema declarations alone are not sufficient when they cannot express the CHECK or partial indexes; the SQL migration and database integration tests are mandatory.

Use targetId only for a real UUID target; for a non-UUID or platform-global target set targetId to null, retain targetType, and store a redacted stable target key in metadata without inventing a UUID or tenant.

U3B must introduce a dedicated append-only AuditEventOutbox table as the durable retry channel. After a business rollback, the service first attempts an isolated AuditLog transaction; if that write fails while the database can accept the outbox transaction, it atomically enqueues the redacted canonical event outside the rolled-back business transaction with the same idempotency key and payload digest required by auditlog_idempotency_authority. A worker claims rows in created_at order, retries with bounded exponential backoff, inserts or resolves the final AuditLog event through the shared database idempotency primitive, treats only same-key/same-digest delivery as duplicate success, and marks delivered rows. Pending rows are never time-purged, delivered receipts are retained for at least 30 days, and dead-letter evidence is retained for at least 24 months or longer under legal/security hold. Outbox payloads follow the same redaction prohibition as AuditLog and contain no secrets or complete request bodies. If neither AuditLog nor the outbox can durably commit, the endpoint returns HTTP 503 with the correlation ID and never reports mutation success; an operational alert is required. Tests must prove the business transaction rolled back, the outbox row committed independently, replay creates exactly one audit event, retries preserve ordering per correlation ID, same-digest duplicates are harmless, conflicting digests fail closed, redaction and retention hold, and the 503 path cannot be mistaken for success.

DELETE /api/v1/superadmin/tenants/:id implements logical deletion under accepted ADR-023: production code changes the retained Tenant status to deleted and must not call tenant.delete or tenant.deleteMany. Every deletion attempt is also a PLATFORM-scoped immutable lifecycle event, for both success and failure: tenantId is null, targetType is tenant, targetId is the real tenant UUID (the field has no Tenant foreign key), and metadata contains only a redacted pre-delete snapshot allowlist (tenant UUID, non-secret display label or hash, prior status, request/correlation ID, actor role, outcome, and stable failure code). The successful status transition and PLATFORM event commit atomically; a failed transition rolls back first and its PLATFORM event is written through the isolated AuditLog/outbox mechanism. The deletion event is retained for at least 24 months and longer under legal/security hold. A later controlled physical purge is prohibited until the retention window expires, required evidence is archived, and no hold exists; the non-FK PLATFORM event remains retained and is excluded from tenant cascade and ordinary cleanup. U3B tests must prove logical-delete success evidence remains queryable, failure evidence survives rollback, a test-only forced Tenant cascade cannot remove the PLATFORM event, retention cleanup cannot remove it early, and no placeholder tenant or actor tenant is stored.

Tenant.status = deleted is a terminal fail-closed operational state. The shared server-side authentication and authorization boundary must re-read the retained Tenant status on every authenticated request (within-request caching is allowed, token/session claims alone are not) and reject member, leader, and operator access on their next request, including already-issued sessions; product APIs return a stable TENANT_DELETED denial and authenticated pages end the tenant session without rendering tenant data. Public tenant resolution also treats deleted as unavailable. Tenant-owned work must check status both when it is claimed and immediately before any external or billable side effect: background jobs, queued autonomous/agent work, scheduled messages, AI execution, publishing, automation, and webhooks are cancelled or skipped with a stable deleted-tenant reason and must not mutate data, send messages, call providers, or reactivate the tenant. A provider webhook may acknowledge only as its protocol requires after durable redacted suppression evidence; it may never change deleted back to active. A platform_admin may read the retained tombstone through the explicit superadmin forensic endpoint, but ordinary PATCH returns TENANT_DELETED_TERMINAL and cannot restore it. Restore is prohibited in OS 3.8; any future restore requires a separate endpoint, reviewed ADR/task, exact authorization, and success/failure audit evidence. DELETE uses a database conditional transition or row lock: exactly one concurrent request changes status, while losers re-read deleted and return the same terminal no-op response. A retry with the same idempotency key reuses its original result/evidence; each independent repeated attempt is auditable without another state transition. U3B tests must cover an already-issued session, member/leader/operator APIs, public resolution, claim-time and pre-side-effect deletion races, scheduled/queued/AI/webhook suppression, late paid webhook non-reactivation, ordinary PATCH rejection, platform forensic read, repeated DELETE, same-key retry, and concurrent DELETE.

U3B adds dedicated nullable AuditLog.idempotencyKey and AuditLog.payloadDigest columns. The reviewed SQL migration creates a unique partial database index on idempotency_key WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL and a CHECK requiring both fields to be null or both to be non-null 64-character lowercase SHA-256 hex values. Existing AuditLog rows are deterministically left with both fields null; no historical identity is invented and null legacy rows never satisfy a replay lookup. Every new superadmin success/failure event and every AuditEventOutbox row must carry both values. Direct AuditLog writes and outbox replay use one shared canonical event builder and database insert/dedupe primitive: idempotencyKey is SHA-256 of versioned RFC 8785 canonical JSON containing correlation ID, scope/tenant marker, action, target type, stable target key, and outcome; payloadDigest is SHA-256 of the complete redacted canonical audit payload excluding delivery timestamps and retry metadata. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on the dedicated key may return the existing event only when its payloadDigest is identical. The same key and same digest is duplicate success; the same key with a different digest never overwrites an event or marks an outbox row delivered, fails closed with AUDIT_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, emits a durable security/operations alert, and dead-letters the conflicting delivery. Real PostgreSQL integration tests must race replay against replay and direct write against replay, prove exactly one final AuditLog row and one stable event ID for equal payloads, prove different-digest conflicts preserve the original row, and inspect the unique index, pairing/hex CHECK, legacy-null behavior, and alert/dead-letter evidence below the application layer.
